jobs.occupation: Tenure track Assistant professor/Associate professor Position in Materials Science and Engineering
jobs.description:
Aarhus University, Denmark

The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering at Aarhus University invites applications for two positions at the rank of:

•   Tenure Track Assistant Professor, or

•   Associate Professor

The positions are offered within the broad field of Materials Engineering and Manufacturing, with a particular focus on participating in the department’s research and education in materials engineering, durability, emerging and advanced materials, advanced manufacturing and surface engineering. The department seeks candidates who will help shape a modern materials science profile, in research as well as in teaching, and who have demonstrated relevant experience in the field.

Expected start date

July 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible.

Research Areas

We welcome applicants with a solid background in materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, materials-focused chemical engineering, applied physics, or closely related disciplines.

We particularly encourage applications within, but not limited to, the following research themes:

Additive and hybrid manufacturing

Including metal additive manufacturing, laser-based processing and welding, joining of metallic and dissimilar materials, post-processing, surface engineering, and process characterisation and modelling.

Materials durability and advanced materials

Including materials under demanding and extreme conditions, 4D printing, bioprinting, and biofabrication, surface modification, lubrication technologies and functional surfaces.

Applicants are expected to contribute to both fundamental understanding and applied solutions, with relevance to engineering systems and industrial applications

Research and Teaching Responsibilities

The selected candidates will:

•   Teach, contribute to, and develop courses in materials science and engineering, additive manufacturing, and manufacturing processes at different levels, from foundational bachelor’s courses to specialized master’s and PhD courses

•   Contribute directly to the further development of the materials and manufacturing science curriculum at different program levels

•   Supervise bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD students

•   Attract external research funding

•   Engage in knowledge exchange with industry and research partners

•   Participate in departmental and university service activities

Your Profile

We are looking for candidates who can contribute to research, education, and innovation at an international level.

To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:

-   A PhD in materials science and engineering, mechanical engineering, or a closely related field

-   Substantial experience conducting high-quality research in materials science and engineering, with publications in leading international journals that match career stage

-   Experience in at least one of the research areas listed above, along with familiarity with experimental, computational, or theoretical research methods

-   Interest in interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering disciplines and with industry

-   For the positions as associate professor, the applicants should, in addition, have:

-   Documented teaching experience and a clear commitment to teaching and advancing materials science courses, from introductory undergraduate instruction through master’s and PhD-level study

-   For associate professor applicants: a documented record of self-directed research leadership, external funding acquisition, supervision of PhD students, and teaching and course development at university level

Who we are

The engineering field in Aarhus University is evolving with a rapid growth in student population, major research initiatives as well as through the establishment of a number of new physical facilities in the city center of Aarhus. We have comprehensive plans for increased activities in research and education, as well as public and industrial cooperation. The  Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering  within the Faculty of Technical Sciences has cooperation with universities and advisory service providers in more than 20 countries. The engineering field at Aarhus University is well established with extensive research activities, over 700 mechanical engineering students and a long tradition of industrial cooperation that we wish to extend significantly.

What we offer

The department offers:

-   research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

-   an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

-   a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

-   a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

-   a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance

Place of work and area of employment

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Mechanical and Production Engineering, Katrinebjergvej 89, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contact information

For more information about the position contact Head of Section of Manufacturing and Mechatronics, Professor Ramin Aghababaei (ra@mpe.au.dk / +45 9350 8956)

or Head of Section of Mechanics and Materials, Professor Michal Kazimierz Budzik (mibu@mpe.au.dk, +45 4189 3217)

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than December 8th, 2026.

Technical Sciences Tenure Track

Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship.

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level

• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists

• to create transparency in the academic career path

As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure

• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training

• a mentoring programme

• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level

As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Senior Director - Global Service Sales M/F
jobs.description:
Are you ready to take the commercial lead of a global Service business and drive its next phase of profitable growth?

KK’s Service business generates approximately DKK 800m in annual revenue and is an increasingly important contributor to the company’s growth and profitability. To build on this strong foundation, we are looking for a Senior Director, Global Service Sales to lead our international Service Sales organisation across Denmark, Spain, the USA and China.

In this role, you will have overall responsibility for driving profitable growth across the Service business. You will set the commercial direction, strengthen key customer relationships and further develop our sales capabilities, while ensuring strong execution across pricing, pipeline management and business development.

Reporting to the VP Service, you will be a key member of the Service leadership team and play an important role in shaping the future direction and continued growth of the business.

Purpose of position:

We are looking for a commercially driven leader who combines strategic thinking with strong execution and people leadership.

You know how to set a clear direction and turn commercial ambitions into results. At the same time, you stay close to customers, markets and your organisation, giving you a strong understanding of where the opportunities are and what it takes to capture them.

As a leader, you create clarity, accountability and momentum. You build strong teams, empower people to take ownership and bring the organisation with you as the business continues to grow.

Responsibilities

As Senior Director, Global Service Sales, you will have overall responsibility for driving the commercial development and performance of our global Service business. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Define and execute the commercial strategy for the Service business, driving sustainable and profitable growth across markets

• Identify and develop new business opportunities while strengthening KK’s aftermarket and Service offering

• Build and maintain strong relationships with key customers and strategic stakeholders

• Strengthen pricing discipline, commercial decision-making and account management across regions

• Build a strong sales pipeline and improve forecasting, commercial planning and performance follow-up

• Translate market developments, customer needs and competitive insights into concrete commercial opportunities

• Lead, develop and motivate an international sales organisation across Denmark, Spain, the USA and China

• Build a strong performance culture with clear accountability, customer focus and commercial excellence

• Develop commercial capabilities and future leaders while ensuring the organisation is equipped for continued growth

• Work closely with Service Operations, Engineering, Project Management and other functions to ensure strong commercial execution

• Drive collaboration and knowledge sharing across regions and act as a visible and trusted member of the Service leadership team.

Our Requirements

We are looking for a commercially driven leader with a strong track record of delivering growth through people, customer relationships and business development.

You will likely bring:

• Significant experience in senior commercial or sales leadership roles, ideally from Service, Aftermarket or other similar recurring revenue businesses. Experience within the wind industry is advantageous.

• Responsibility for delivering profitable growth in an international business

• Experience leading teams across multiple countries and cultures

• Strong commercial acumen and strategic thinking

• A proven ability to build customer relationships at senior levels

• Experience operating successfully in a matrix organisation

• A structured and data-driven approach to sales management

Would you like to lead a team of scientists and help turn scientific expertise into reliable QC delivery? Join Bavarian Nordic as Manager of the Biochemistry scientist team and support the quality of vaccines that help protect lives around the world.

**Your team and leadership environment

**Biochemistry consists of 10 laboratory technicians and nine scientists organised across two teams. In this role, you will lead the scientist team and work closely with colleagues across the area.

The area performs analytical testing of raw materials, intermediates, finished products, process development samples, stability samples and control cells for extraneous agents. Techniques include physico-chemical testing, ELISA, HPLC and hemadsorption assays. Biochemistry also performs method development, validation and comparability testing.

You will join a QC department of approximately 90 employees across six teams. Our Core Leadership Team of Senior Managers works closely with First-Line Managers, the Operational Excellence Partner and a Quality Integrator to develop people and processes and maintain strong quality oversight.

QC is undergoing significant change as we support increased production demands, improve efficiency and reduce lead times. As a first-line manager, you will translate changing priorities into clear direction while maintaining employee engagement, well-being and a strong quality mindset.

**Your Responsibilities

**

• Lead and develop the scientist team. Provide clear direction, regular feedback and individual development planning. Coach your scientists, strengthen competencies and create psychological safety while holding the team accountable for high-quality results.

• Balance scientific and operational priorities. Maintain an overview of the scientists’ workload and operational risks. Align priorities across routine analytical activities, method development, validation and comparability testing, adjusting plans as QC and manufacturing needs change.

• Ensure quality and robust processes. Ensure the team’s work complies with cGMP and the Bavarian Nordic Quality Management System. Promote data integrity, accurate documentation and inspection readiness, and help maintain robust processes across the analytical sample lifecycle.

• Strengthen collaboration and improvement. Work closely with the laboratory technician team and stakeholders across QC and manufacturing. Use data and digital tools to improve coordination, address bottlenecks and support efficient analytical workflows and reduced lead times.

**Your profile

**

• You are a people-oriented leader who can support scientific specialists, create structure and maintain momentum in a changing GMP environment. You enjoy developing others and connecting scientific work with operational priorities.

• A relevant scientific degree and experience from a GMP-regulated pharmaceutical or biotechnology environment, preferably within QC biochemistry or analytical testing.

• An understanding of analytical methods and experience relevant to method development, validation or comparability testing.

• Leadership experience from QC, a laboratory or a similar area is an advantage, with the ability to coach specialists and support their professional growth.

• A solid understanding of cGMP, data integrity and Quality Management Systems, and confidence using LIMS or other digital laboratory tools.

• An ability to prioritise competing activities, communicate expectations clearly and build effective relationships across scientific and operational teams.

**Why join Bavarian Nordic

**You will lead a scientist team whose expertise supports vaccine quality and reliable manufacturing. You will have the opportunity to develop people, strengthen scientific collaboration and influence how Biochemistry delivers both routine activities and analytical improvements.

You will join a leadership team that values coaching, employee development and shared problem-solving. In a department undergoing change, you can contribute to continuous improvement and Operational Excellence while developing professionally in an international vaccine company.

**Ready to make a difference? Apply now!

**Apply by clicking the ‘APPLY’ button. We are interviewing on an ongoing basis and look forward to receiving your CV.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

**For us, it is all about improving and saving lives

**Improving and saving lives through innovative vaccines is at the heart of what we do at Bavarian Nordic. We are a fully integrated vaccine company focused on the development, manufacturing and commercialisation of life-saving vaccines, and the largest pure-play vaccine company in the world.

_Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

__Bavarian Nordic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

_For more information, visit _www.bavarian-nordic.com

jobs.occupation: Graduate - Technology Risk | Autumn 2027 (Aarhus and Copenhagen)

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

What if we didn’t focus on who you are now, but who you could become?

Are you ready to shape the future? Join us at EY as a Graduate in Technology Risk, starting August 2027. We focus on your potential and provide a supportive environment to enhance your professional and personal skills.

The opportunity: your next adventure awaits

As a Graduate in Technology Risk, you will join our Assurance team and work closely with IT managers, CFOs, CTOs, and CISOs across industries. Our team consists of 35 colleagues with diverse educational and cultural backgrounds.

We are looking for analytical and structured individuals with an interest in IT audits, information security, risk management, and IT strategy. Your work will include:

• 
IT audits and risk assessments: Interview stakeholders, understand business and IT processes, test controls, analyse documentation and data, and contribute to reports and recommendations.

• 
IT General Controls and IT Environment Audits: Evaluate IT controls and identify risks related to financial reporting, compliance, and governance frameworks such as ISO 27001 and COBIT.

• 
Service Provider and Technical Platform Audits: Assess controls across service providers, operating systems, databases, and networks.

• 
Data Protection and Security: Support clients with GDPR compliance, information security assessments, and security maturity evaluations.

• 
Technical Platform Audits: Conduct technical reviews of operating systems, databases, and networks, linking technical aspects to business processes.

• 
Emerging Risk Areas: Work with topics such as AI, cybersecurity, cloud governance, DORA, NIS2, ESG, and third-party risk management.

We offer a range of experiences to help you grow in a personalized manner, fostering a culture of global teamwork. You will be surrounded by dedicated colleagues in an inclusive environment, with opportunities for social events to strengthen team cohesion.

Our internal coaching and training programs will equip you with the skills needed to remain relevant in the future, while you build a network of colleagues and mentors at EY.

To learn more about our various teams within Assurance, please visit our career page.

What we look for

• 
You have a growth-focused mindset. We value how you absorb information, learn and take action just as much as the skills you have gained through education and experience.

• 
You are curious and purpose-driven. You see opportunities rather than obstacles and ask insightful questions that help build a better working world.

• 
You are inclusive. You are actively seeking and valuing diverse perspectives, appreciating differences, and collaborating to create a foundation of safety and trust.

• 
Qualifications:

• 

• You completed your studies in 2026 or are set to graduate in 2027.

• 

• You speak and write English fluently.

• 

• You hold, or expect to complete before joining, a relevant master’s degree within IT, information security, auditing, finance, data science, cybersecurity or a related field. You speak and write both Danish and English fluently, enabling you to communicate clearly with clients and colleagues.

What’s in it for you

• 
An exciting introductory program with all new graduates in the Nordics.

• 
A safe onboarding by your own personal buddy and counselor.

• 
Flexible and hybrid-working conditions, so you can make a meaningful impact, your way.

• 
Highly collaborative teams and great support of a network of knowledgeable colleagues.

• 
Continuous development and opportunities to grow your own career through learnings and experiences. A structured learning journey with on-the-job coaching and opportunities to work toward relevant professional certifications.

What you can expect

If you find this position interesting and recognize yourself in the description above, we would like to hear from you as soon as possible. Application deadline: 15 November 2026.

The steps in our recruitment process are as follows:

• 
Application: Submit your cover letter, CV and most recent grade transcript.

• 
Assessment: After submitting your application, you will receive a link to our assessment within a few days. The assessment takes approximately 20 minutes and must be completed by 18 November.

• 
Video: Following the assessment, you are required to complete a brief video interview consisting of three questions outlining your motivation for this role. You can complete this at your convenience; however, it must be submitted by 22 November.

• 
Interview: Selected candidates will be invited to face-to-face interviews on an ongoing basis.

Please note that only applicants who have completed the assessment and video will be considered for the position. We look forward to receiving your application!

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in RNA function and gene regulation
jobs.description:
The laboratory of Ulf Vang Ørom is inviting applications for a 2-year postdoctoral position at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics at Aarhus University.

The position will focus on RNA and its role in regulating cellular pathways relevant for metabolic processes.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from February 1 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter with possibility for extension of the employment.

Job description
You will be working using several methods to study RNA, protein-interactions and epigenetics, often including high through-put methods. The project focuses on novel aspects linking RNA, metabolism and epigenetics, and allows for active involvement in shaping the project within its duration. You will be working with a high degree of independence and in collaboration with other researchers at the institute and internationally.

Your profile
Applicants should have a PhD degree in a relevant area and expertise with working with RNA and high through-put methods.

Applicant should have a high-quality publication record and excellent language (English) skills.

Who we are
The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (https://mbg.au.dk/en/) hosts researchers in the areas of RNA and protein biology, bioinformatics and nutrition, as well as plant research, giving great opportunities for interdisciplinary collaborations.

What we offer 
The department offers

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Universitetsbyen 81, 8000 Aarhus, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments. 

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Ulf Vang Ørom, PhD, +45 22288766

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 30 November 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

VP of Quantum - Diasense ApS

Reports to: Marvin Holten, Founder and CTO

Team: Quantum Lead, Quantum Engineers, and part-time specialists in quantum information science and quantum optics, growing through 2027

Location: Quantum Denmark, Copenhagen, Denmark. On-site.

Start: January 2027

Company Overview

Diasense is a deep-tech company turning fundamental quantum physics into world-class scientific instruments. We are building the world's most sensitive magnetic microscope, using nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond to measure magnetic fields at a sensitivity that no other technique can reach.

We are applying that instrument to one of the hardest measurement problems in semiconductor manufacturing: seeing what is actually happening inside a finished chip, electrically and non-destructively. It is a market where the physics has to be exceptional and the engineering has to be industrial, and very few companies in the world are attempting both.

We are a spin-out of DTU Physics, based in the quantum center of Copenhagen, and we are about to move from a working prototype to instruments installed at customers’ sites. The team today is eight full-time and six part-time people. Over 2027 and 2028, we are building that to around thirty. By joining now, you will be one of the people who decide what this company becomes, not someone who inherits it.

Position Overview

Job Description

We are looking for the person who will own the quantum side of our instrument, outright.

You will lead our quantum function: a Quantum Lead, quantum engineers, and part-time specialists, growing over the next eighteen months. You are an experimentalist at heart. We are not looking for someone who manages a lab from a desk. We are looking for the person other physicists go to when something does not work, and nobody can say why. Today that person is our CTO, and your role is to change that. When the quantum work gets stuck, it should stop with you.

You will be joining at the transition point where the instrument moves from lab to customer sites. The physics has to keep improving, and it now also has to withstand contact with the real world. Both halves of that are yours.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Ownership of the Quantum Platform

• 
Own the performance of the NV-diamond measurement chain end to end: optical read-out, microwave control, sensitivity, noise floor and measurement protocols.

• 
Set the technical direction for how we push sensitivity and measurement speed over the next two years.

• 
Make the calls on where the physics effort goes, and be accountable for them.

Hands-on Experimental Work

• 
Spend the majority of your week in the lab, on the instrument, with your hands on it.

• 
Diagnose and fix the problems that have no procedure attached - the ones where the measurement is wrong and nobody yet knows why.

• 
Develop and prove new experimental protocols, rather than reviewing someone else's.

Leading and Building the Quantum Team

• 
Lead the quantum function: our Quantum Lead, quantum engineers and part-time academic specialists, with further hires planned through 2027.

• 
Raise what the team can do unaided. Success looks like fewer problems reaching you over time, not more.

• 
Own hiring for the quantum team as it grows, together with the CTO.

Instruments in the Field

• 
Take technical responsibility for the quantum performance of instruments installed at customer sites.

• 
Support and eventually supervise measurement campaigns at customer locations, so that deployment does not depend on the founders.

• 
Work closely with instrumentation, software and applications colleagues - this instrument only works when all four disciplines agree.

Qualifications & Experience

• 
A PhD in Physics, Quantum Optics, Atomic Physics or a closely related field, followed by substantial further experimental experience in academia or industry.

• 
Deep, sustained, hands-on experimental physics. Years at the bench, building and debugging experiments yourself. This is the single most important qualification and we will test for it.

• 
A demonstrable record of solving unfamiliar, hard experimental problems without supervision. We are interested in what you did when the standard approach failed.

• 
Experience guiding, mentoring or leading other researchers or engineers - formally or informally. You do not need to have held a management title, but you do need to want this half of the job.

• 
An inquisitive and stubborn mindset: willing to question assumptions, including your own, and to keep going after a problem that has already resisted three attempts.

• 
Fluency in Python or MATLAB for research-grade data analysis.

Experience with one or more of the following is a significant advantage:

• 
Cold atoms or trapped ions. Our techniques originate in cold-atom physics rather than in quantum sensing, and we have found that people trained in that tradition tend to carry exactly the debugging instinct this role needs.

• 
Magnetometry, especially with NV centres, and precision measurements.

• 
Microwave electronics and real-time control systems.

• 
Building complex free-space optical systems from components.

• 
Taking a laboratory technique out of the laboratory.

Compensation & Benefits

• 
A competitive salary package.

• 
An attractive warrant package. You will share directly in what you build, and at this stage the share is meaningful.

• 
Relocation support for you and your family, and assistance with the Danish researcher tax scheme, which for qualifying international hires taxes salary at a flat 32.84 percent for up to seven years.

• 
Denmark's quantum ecosystem at your door: DTU Physics, the Niels Bohr Institute and one of Europe's densest concentrations of quantum research.

• 
A small, senior team where decisions are made in a conversation rather than in a process.

USP's for this job

• 
You are the ceiling, not waiting for one. In most companies, the deepest technical authority sits above you, and you work within it. Here you are being hired to become it. The quantum direction of this instrument will be yours.

• 
Lead a team without leaving the lab. Almost every physicist who moves into leadership loses the bench. This role is explicitly designed so that you do not - the leadership comes from being the best experimentalist, not from stopping being one.

• 
Build the Unprecedented: You will be a leading the development and rollout of the most powerful magnetic microscope in the world, directly pushing the boundaries of scientific measurement.

• 
It leaves the building. Our instruments are going into customer laboratories. You will see your work measured by whether it survives in somebody else's fab, which is a rarer and more satisfying test than a paper.

• 
Early enough to matter. Fourteen people today, around thirty by the end of 2028. The people joining now set how this company works.

Do you want to work for an Architectural Firm with sustainability at the heart of its strategy? Can you contribute with solutions from your academic studies? Are you currently studying to be an Construction Architecture (Bygningskonstruktør)? Then, join us to shape a sustainable and liveable world.

About us

Arkitema was established in 1969 making us one of Denmark's oldest architectural firms. Today, we are well positioned in Scandinavia with offices in Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

In our markets we provide wide range of competencies in our areas of expertise. We cover sectors and disciplines like healthcare, industry, transformation, landscape and residential construction.

Since 2019 Arkitema has been part of COWI, one of Scandinavia’s leading engineering and consultancy companies. Together with customers, partners and colleagues, we shape a future where people and societies grow and flourish. We do that by co-creating more sustainable and beautiful solutions that improve the quality of life for people today and many generations ahead.

Create Solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

As an intern at Arkitema, you will be part of a design team in one of Scandinavia's largest and leading architectural firms, where you will work with experienced architects, construction architects, urban planners and engineers to solve a wide range of professionally relevant tasks.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• To use your academic knowledge of technical fundamentals to contribute to our projects

• Gain valuable experience in the field of architecture and construction

Also, you will be included in a team and assigned an experienced colleague as a mentor who will guide you throughout your internship. We carry out architecture primarily throughout the Nordic region but also other parts of the world within the areas of; Housing, Learning, Business, Health, Urban, Culture and Infrastructure. Therefore, our assignments range from small preservation-worthy residential neighborhoods to complex super hospitals, bridges and cultural centers.

As an intern, you will have the opportunity to be involved in drawing the first lines, registering old building masses, supervising construction sites on ongoing projects, or modeling and detailing the many complex buildings. Our professional span will give you a broad understanding of the design profession and in-depth knowledge of the workflows in the construction industry.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners, or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

On top of that, you’ll have:

• Actively pursuing a bachelor’s degree in architectural technology and construction management (Bygningskonstruktør)

• Have good problem-solving skills

• Be a creative and technical thinker

• Be able to demonstrate evidence of research and information gathering skills

Professional development

We strive to develop talented interns who graduate with a high level of professional skills. As part of the internship at Arkitema, there are ongoing presentations where our own specialists share their experience and best practices in topics such as:

• Sustainability, materials & reuse

• BIM, Revit, design & sketching

• Client consultancy & tendering

• Restoration & building preservation

• Competitions & visualizations

• Descriptions & quality assurance

• Urban Planning

These topics represent important knowledge and practical insights that will ensure you stand stronger in your future career.

A place to work and so much more

At Arkitema, we work together with our customers to shape sustainable and customized solutions. By making use of our collective knowledge and curiosity, we create opportunities that contribute to good solutions for a future with ever-changing needs.

We want to develop an environment where curiosity, belonging and good chemistry are in focus.

For us, it is important that the people we share everyday work with are allowed to be themselves, precisely because it is what brings out the best in you and those around us, both at work and at home.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role, please reach out Jacob Faaborg-Simonsen – jafs@arkitema.com for Aarhus/Aalborg and Adrian Balch Petersen – adpn@arkitema.com for Copenhagen.

Get to know us even better at our website, Arkitema where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at Arkitema.

Diversity is fundamental to Arkitema, inclusion is key.

We focus on creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equal opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are considered valuable. We also take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes when we put together teams and forums. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

NOTE

Kindly submit your CV, Cover Letter, and Portfolio. As only two attachment fields are available on the application page, please combine files where needed and upload them accordingly.

We only accept applications from active students who have not already completed an internship within their studies.

jobs.occupation: Opslag 170259 Professor or Associate Professor and Research Group Leader with special focus on molecular mechanisms of diabetes
jobs.description:
Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC), University of Copenhagen

   

  BRIC wishes to recruit a strongly motivated scientist at Associate Professor or Professor level for an independent research group leader position. We are seeking excellent candidates with ambitious research visions within translational diabetes type 1 or 2 research and a drive to contribute to a diverse and inspiring research environment. The research group leader position is combined with a senior researcher position at the Bartholin Institute, Department of Pathology, Centre for Diagnostics, Rigshospitalet, Capital Region. The start date is 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  It is a requirement for the appointment that the applicant is accepted for both the research group leader position and the senior researcher position. In order to be considered, the applicant must send two applications: one to the faculty (the research group leader position) and one to the hospital (the senior researcher position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the senior researcher position. This also applies to applicants who are already employed at the Hospital. The advertisement for the senior researcher position is available here

  The workplace
 BRIC is an international center of excellence with the mission to perform cutting-edge basic and translational biomedical research in an open environment that fosters interdisciplinarity and collaboration. Active research areas include many aspects of cancer biology, stem cell biology and neurobiology. The center is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. 

  Job description
 As a group leader, you will establish an independent research program within translational diabetes research. Your capacity to integrate research and clinical perspectives is emphasized. In the job, you will be expected to:

   	
• Conduct, publish, and communicate high-quality research that moves the field forward 	
• Engage in outreach and knowledge-sharing with society 	
• Develop your research group through attraction of competitive funding and talent development of team members 	
• Conduct research-based teaching and examination 	
• Be involved in academic assessments 	
• Be involved in local as well as international collaborative and multidisciplinary research projects and engage in core center activities such as talent or technology development to advance BRIC’s research environment and culture   You are also expected to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills and to contribute to developing the research environment and culture at BRIC.

  50 % of the working time is employment at Copenhagen University and will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g., research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Director at the Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC). The remaining time will be allocated for other tasks at the Bartholin Institute and the Department of Pathology (e.g. research administration, personnel responsibility, methods establishment and development, grant writing and the establishment of a competitive research group) in agreement with the Head of the Bartholin Institute.

  Candidate profile
 Your background includes a PhD degree, postdoctoral training, and a track record documenting your research experience as reflected in a strong publication record matching your career stage. Also desired is a successful record of attraction of funds, leadership and educational experiences, collaboration experiences and additional capabilities within areas such as outreach or technology transfer activities, again reflecting your career stage.  

  We offer

   	
• Access to cutting edge technologies through core facilities, including high-content screening, flow cytometry, next-gen sequencing, bioinformatics, microscopy, single cell genomics, histology and access to spatial transcriptomics and pathology services. Additional core facilities are available at faculty level. 	
• A vibrant and open scientific community with focus on collegiality, collaboration and creativity.  	
• A focus on talent training and development at all career stages, including strong PhD and postdoc programs. 	
• Strategic support for funding strategizing, grant writing and implementation of larger grants and collaborations and for research communication and outreach. 	
• A package covering the salary of 1-2 group members and technical support equivalent to 50 % of a full-time technical position from the Bartholin Institute. 	
• Administrative support with regards to laboratory services and safety, purchase, economy, HR, and IT. 	
• Additional start support may be obtained from private foundations (obtained at individual or center level).   Terms of employment
 Initial appointment as group leader (Associate Professor) is for 6 years.

  BRIC wants to offer a further career path pending a positive evaluation following transparent guidelines, which include the UCPH criteria for recognizing merit

  This can happen in form of employment in a permanent position based on public advertisement, or the group leader may enter the University of Copenhagen Promotion Program towards a position as full professor (permanent position). Experienced research leaders may be recruited at the level of full professor. 

  The average weekly working hours in the combined position are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations. 

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Additional information about BRIC can be found on www.bric.ku.dk

  Inquiries are welcome to Director Anders H. Lund bric-director@bric.ku.dk

  Recruitment process
 The recruitment process will contain four evaluation steps: 

   	
• After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager will shortlist applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointment Committee after an evaluation of the written application material. Evaluation criteria can be seen here. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. Due to differences in career stage or institutional background, not all candidates are required to fulfil all requirements in full. 	
• The Vice Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. The selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. 	
• Selected candidates will be evaluated in an online interview with the Appointment committee. The online interviews is expected to be carried out between late January and early February  	
• Selected candidates will be invited for an on-site visit and final evaluation in late February    

  To be qualified for a Professor or Associate Professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion..

  You can read about the recruitment process here: Recruitment process  – University of Copenhagen.

  Application material

   	
• Cover letter outlining the applicant’s motivation to apply to BRIC and brief summaries of research visions (1 page). 	
• Application dossier (10 pages) 	 		
• Research vision/goal and synergy with BRIC 		
• Current and future research plan 		
• Description of five most significant contributions (e.g., scientific, clinical, commercial achievements, honours/awards) 		
• List of funding and commercial income raised incl. information about grant donor, type of grant, amount, and period 		
• Description of leadership experience and development. 		
• Description of organizational activities, including initiatives, responsibilities, and participation in committees and platforms 		
• Teaching portfolio including reflection on teaching and supervision, see guidelines. Selected candidates that do not have the required teaching experience will be given the opportunity to qualify within the first two years of employment. 	 	    	
• CV (2 pages use provided sub-sections) 	
• Diplomas 	
• Complete list of publications/ORCID – please indicate contribution in collaborative papers. Highlight selected publications relevant for research plan and for these include a short description (10 lines) of outcome/impact of the work and your contribution.  	
• Reprints of up to five selected papers (Associate Professor) or ten (Professor) (only published or in press)    

  Please note the level of appointment sought.

  Please note that selected applicants who have applied for either both positions or just the professor position will be assessed for the associate professor position if they are found not-qualified for the professor position.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the Assessment Committee requires further documentation. The Assessment Committee is comprised of employees from both BRIC and Rigshospitalet.
 
 The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 
 
 The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position (see also https://www.bric.ku.dk/career-at-bric)
 
 Please submit the application with the required attachments. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, Thursday, 19 November 2026

  BRIC highly values diversity and encourages people of all backgrounds to apply see also https://www.bric.ku.dk/career-at-bric

  The University of Copenhagen International Staff Mobility Office offers assistance and guidance regarding relocation, e.g., housing, spouse program, pension and taxes, as well as on general information on the Danish society, e.g. child-care, healthcare etc. For more information, visit the ISM website:  https://ism.ku.dk/.

Consultant Interventional Cardiologist – PCI On-Call Service

Department of Cardiology, Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark

The opportunity
Are you an experienced interventional cardiologist looking to join a highly specialised university hospital with a strong clinical, academic and collaborative environment?

The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is seeking one or more Consultant Interventional Cardiologists from the EU/EØS to join our team. We welcome applications from candidates who are already qualified to participate in a PCI on-call service, as well as experienced PCI operators who are motivated to develop the additional competencies required for on-call duties.

The position is available as soon as possible or by mutual agreement.

This is an opportunity to work in a busy interventional cardiology environment, contribute to the development of specialised cardiac care and collaborate with highly skilled colleagues across cardiology, cardiac surgery and other disciplines.

The position
Your primary clinical responsibilities will be within interventional cardiology, particularly percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
The position includes participation in the department's PCI on-call service.

You will be part of a multidisciplinary team providing specialised care for patients with ischaemic heart disease, including patients requiring urgent and complex coronary interventions.
Depending on your experience, qualifications and the department's clinical needs, there may also be opportunities to contribute to the development of other specialised interventional services, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and chronic total occlusion (CTO) procedures.

Alongside your clinical responsibilities, you will contribute to the department's research, teaching and professional development activities, as well as relevant administrative and organisational tasks.

What we offer

• The opportunity to work in a busy university hospital with an established PCI service and a broad range of specialised cardiology services.
• Professional development: Opportunities to further develop your interventional skills and, where appropriate, expand your expertise into complex PCI, TAVI or CTO procedures.
• A strong multidisciplinary team: Close collaboration with cardiologists across subspecialties, cardiothoracic anaesthetists and cardiac surgeons.
• An academic environment: Opportunities to participate in clinical research, teaching and the development of new treatment pathways.
• Supportive colleagues and leadership: We value professional respect, constructive collaboration and a positive working environment.
• Flexible working arrangements: Working hours and duty schedules are organised within the applicable employment framework.
• An international perspective: The opportunity to join a university hospital committed to clinical excellence, research, education and continuous improvement.
Qualifications and experience
Essential requirements

• You hold specialist certification in cardiology.
• You have or are able to obtain a Danish Authorization to practice medicine
• You are fluent in or command a professional working proficiency in Danish. Norwegian or Swedish (B2/C1 level)
• Or are willing to learn Danish
• You can perform PCI procedures independently.
• You have the clinical judgement and professional skills required to manage patients with ischaemic heart disease.
• You communicate effectively and work constructively with colleagues across clinical disciplines.
• You can maintain an overview and make sound clinical decisions in a demanding and sometimes unpredictable environment.
• You are committed to high standards of patient care, patient safety and continuous professional development.
• You are willing to contribute to the department's clinical, organisational and educational activities and to take on the leadership and supervisory responsibilities associated with a consultant position.
Desirable qualifications

• Experience participating in a PCI on-call service.
• Experience from a university hospital or another highly specialised cardiac centre.
• Experience in complex PCI, TAVI or CTO procedures.
• A PhD, or other research qualifications or a strong record of scientific publications.
• Experience in clinical research, teaching or quality improvement.
• Experience in a PCI on-call service is an advantage but is not essential, provided you are an independent PCI operator and are motivated to acquire the necessary competencies following an appropriate period of training and induction.
About the Department
The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is a large, specialised and research-active department providing advanced care across a broad range of cardiovascular conditions, including ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, valvular heart disease, thoracic aortic aneurysms, pericardial diseases, thromboembolic disorders and dyslipidaemia.

Our department performs approximately:

• 6,000 invasive procedures annually
• 8,000 inpatient admissions annually
• More than 30,000 outpatient consultations annually
• Approximately 14,000 echocardiographic examinations annually
Our medical team comprises doctors at different stages of postgraduate training and 32 consultant cardiologists, including two professors.
We provide inpatient and outpatient services, operate a cardiac catheterisation laboratory and maintain a dedicated cardiology research unit.
Our work is guided by a shared commitment to clinical excellence, patient safety and involving patients and their families in shared decision-making. We also have a strong responsibility for undergraduate medical education and postgraduate specialist training.
The department operates across three hospital sites in Aalborg, Thisted and Hobro, with the vast majority of clinical activity based at the newly built Aalborg University Hospital.

Salary and terms of employment
This is a full-time position. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the applicable Danish collective agreement.
The position includes participation in the department's PCI on-call service.
Further details regarding the on-call arrangement and employment conditions can be discussed with the Head of Department or Lead Senior Physician Bent Raungaard tlf. 27201096, e-mail: b.raungaard@rn.dk
 
Application
Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and interviews will be arranged continuously. The advertisement will be withdrawn once the position has been filled.
Please submit your application by email to:
Ljubica Vukelic Andersen
Head of Department of Cardiology
Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark
Email: ljubica.andersen@rn.dk
Telephone: +45 30 38 25 10

Please include:

• Curriculum Vitae (CV).
• Letter of motivation
• Proof of specialist certification in cardiology.
• List of publications, if applicable.
The assessment process will follow the applicable Danish requirements for consultant appointments, including assessment of competencies across the seven physician roles.

jobs.occupation: Internship in Embedded Software Development for Electricity Meters
jobs.description:
Do you have a passion for software programming and are you up for new challenges? Would you like to be part of developing the future’s electricity meters for automated reading systems? Are you interested in an exciting and educational internship at an international green-tech company?

Here is what your role entails

During this internship you will become a part of a Scrum team working with embedded software for electricity meters, as well as the scripts and tools that tie the development process together. Your daily task includes improving and extending automated test software, maintaining test setups based on Raspberry Pi, and participating in proof-of-concept development projects. The specific content of the tasks will be planned together with you based on your preferences, interests, and competencies.

There is a wide range of technical disciplines, and some of the tools you might work with include:

• Python

• Programmering i C

• C#

• GIT

• Automatic software test

• DevOps

Meet your future team

As an intern in Embedded Software Development - Electricity Meters, you’ll become an integral part of our meter development department. This department designs and maintains hardware and software for our metering systems. You will join a team of 8 skilled development engineers, all with a background in firmware development and testing. Collaboration is a key focus, and close interaction with experienced colleagues provides ample opportunities for daily discussions, professional growth, and a steep learning curve during your internship.

Did you know? Our team does not just collaborate at work — we also team up on the padel court!

Less about us, more about you

We are looking for a motivated student interested in software development, who values quality and high reliability in our solutions.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Are studying a degree in electronics engineering or a related field

• Are flexible, structured, and enjoy working closely with your colleagues

• Have a can-do mindset that enables you to take on new and challenging tasks

• Are driven by a passion for developing software

As we are an international organisation it is important that you are fluent in English and Danish.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, this is an internship position, and we value curiosity and a willingness to learn just as much as experience. If the role interests you and you are motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply.

We offer more than just an internship

At Kamstrup, your contribution as an intern is highly valued, and we cherish the good colleagueship. Therefore, you will experience an internship with a strong focus on your individual development through challenging tasks, career sparring, voluntary courses, as well as social events and a large network. We are proud, that our internship program has resulted in Studenterhus Aarhus granting us with the Mentor Award, the Internationalization Award, the Jury’s Special Award and the award for East Jutland’s Best Internship.

Besides the best program, we also offer:

• The internship is paid if your place of study allows it

• Multiple internship events and weekly internship lunches

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association, that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

The applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, but you can expect a response within six weeks. Any details about the internship will be individually agreed upon. However, the internship is expected to run from the beginning of February 2026 until the end of June 2026.

Kamstrup is located in Stilling south of Aarhus, and bus number 200 takes you right to the door.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Team lead, Jesper Kristensen on telephone nr.: (+45) 89 93 10 00.
